title: Intent conforms to the dev, opt and brew contract
objective:
Intent follows the one dev, opt and brew contract every tool released through Homebrew follows (devbin's `docs/dev-opt-brew.md`, landed at Devbin commit aeed31e4 and amended by devbin issues 0213 and 0216), so that a maintainer moves between the checkout, a published working copy and the Homebrew keg with one switch, every tree names itself the same way, and a user's `brew install` keeps working without ever running the switch.

Concretely:

1. One function in intentsvcs names the running tree, brew, opt, dev or unknown, from the manifest and git, and every caller asks it; `intent --version`, `intent version` and doctor print the contract's one line, `intent <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty]) at <root> <provenance>`, with the sha the commit the running pair was built from.
2. `intent install [--prefix <dir>] [--force] [--managed-by brew]` publishes the runtime set from dev into a prefix and writes the manifest `<root>/.intent-install` in the contract's exact form; a dirty runtime set, a prefix another tool wrote, and any tree but dev are refused by name.
3. `intent use [dev|opt|brew]` points the per-user link set, `intent` and `intentd` in `~/.local/bin`, at one tree as a pair, removes it for brew, reports the tree each link serves when bare, and ends in `intent daemon restart`; doctor and bare `use` fail the shadow check.
4. The formula installs the signed release assets as today and writes the same manifest with `managed_by: brew`; the keg stays linked, `releasing.md` no longer unlinks and pins it, and a maintainer's path is `intent use`.
5. The proof runs on this machine through dev, opt and brew in turn, and with brew alone on kovacs, each tree printing its line with doctor and the shadow check clean, and devbin's switch proven in this checkout.
context:
On 2026-10-24 hv ruled that Intent, Molt, Utilz and devbin use one identical approach to dev, opt and brew trees, that the spec has one home in devbin's docs, and that the user's links come first on PATH (option B: formulae keep linking into Homebrew's bin, Molt-matts puts `~/.local/bin` ahead of Homebrew's bin on every sleeve, `<tool> use` switches the link set, no link means brew). All four estates said SAME to the contract's draft v0.4 that day, Intent at 06:58Z, with Intent's column measured at e6b784790 (vc, `contract-intent-column.md`, carried into the design attachment here). hv placed this thread third in 3.2.7, after issue 0635 and the devbin v0.1.14 re-vendor (vc decision 71), both now on main; devbin itself conformed in its 0213.

Today Intent's brew keg is unlinked and pinned so that the dev pair symlinked into `~/.local/bin` is the one `intent` on PATH, `intent --version` prints `intent <version> (<sha40>) <provenance>`, there is no manifest, no `install` and no `use`, and the support set is listed once in `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/support.lib`. The design attachment records each of the contract's ten sections against Intent as measured, the deltas, and the hazards the switch cannot see (a launchd-spawned process whose PATH lacks `~/.local/bin` runs brew's copy for Claude Code's hooks and MCP server). ST0081, Intent from Homebrew on Linux and macOS, is the thread this one builds on: its formula and release assets are the brew tree this contract names.

related.note: ST0081's formula and release assets are the brew tree this contract names; this thread's WP-04 changes that formula to write the manifest

wps.title: The tree function, the runtime set and the version line
wps.objective: One function in intentsvcs names the running tree, read in the contract's order (brew when the manifest says `managed_by: brew`; opt when its `tool` is `intent`; dev when the root is a git work tree with no manifest; unknown otherwise, which doctor fails), and every caller asks it. One function lists the runtime set, the pair plus the support paths git names (`lib/templates`, `intent/plugins/claude`, `intent/plugins/agents/plugin.json`), and `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/support.lib` reads that list from the built binary instead of keeping `SUPPORT_PATHS` of its own. The version line becomes `intent <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty]) at <root> <provenance>`: the sha is the commit the running pair was built from, read from the binary and never HEAD at run time; `+dirty` follows it in dev when the support set differs from that commit or the pair was built from a dirty tree, never in opt or brew; `<root>` is absolute, and a brew root is its opt link; the trailing provenance word (`release`, `dev`) stays, which readers of the first four fields ignore. Doctor prints the same line and says when HEAD has moved past the build. Every reader of the old line moves in the same bank: `bin/int`, the devbin commands `macos`, `brew`, `local`, `linux`, `prepush`, `shared/brew.lib`, `shared/releasestamp.lib` and `build.d/release`, the bats files that match the line, the ST0056 parity tools, and the formula's `test do`. Arms: the tree function on each of the four answers from scratch roots; the line's shape and the sha source in dev with a pair built behind HEAD; the dirty marker with a dirty support set.
wps.body:
## Measurements, and the readers that move (cc, 2026-10-25 07:08Z by date -u)

Static measurements from main's tree, taken before the bank; the readers below are driven again against a pair printing the new line at the judge.

- **M1, the runtime set.** It had one definition, `SUPPORT_PATHS` in `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/support.lib`, and the binary held no copy (only `install::MARKER`, the root marker). It is used by `cmd/macos`'s stage (coverage, the coverage loop, `provenance_blockers`, the support asset and its drift check), `cmd/linux`'s package dirt check, `support.lib`'s own `git archive`, and the `macos_release_assets.bats` fixture. `cmd/brew` and `shared/brew.lib` name it only in comments.
- **M2, the readers of the line.** Field 2, the version, survives unchanged: `brew.lib`'s `staged_version`, `build.d/release`'s stamp check, `macos publish` through `staged_version`, and the formula's `test do`. These print or record the whole line and survive too: `brew smoke`, `cmd/linux`'s build and smoke, `prepush` (rc only), the pre-commit hooks' parentheticals, and `burn.sh`'s TSV header. `bin/int` prints devbin's line, not Intent's. The `dirty-` readers under `bin/.devbin` read the embedded `[intent-source-commit:...]` marker, which this bank leaves as it is.
- **M3, `at <root>` for brew.** On this Mac `/opt/homebrew/opt/intent` links to `../Cellar/intent/<version>`, and the binary's real path is under the Cellar, so the root prints through `stable_root`'s Cellar-to-opt mapping. Linux (kovacs) is unmeasured, and that keg is hv's.
- **M4, the provenance word.** No shell reads it: the gate's self-provenance arm and `verify_pair` read the embedded marker. It stays last at no cost.

### What this bank moves

- The two printers, intent-cli's `spine.rs` (with `intent version` in `render.rs`) and intentd's `main.rs`, now call one formatter, `intentsvcs::install::version_line`. The CLI builds the line when it is asked for, not when the Command is, since a dev tree's line reads git.
- `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/gen_explorer_shots.sh`, which split the line by position.
- The Rust pins `intent-cli/tests/version_spellings_agree.rs` and `intentd/tests/arguments_do_not_start_a_daemon.rs`.
- The bats fixtures: `macos_release_assets.bats` reads the list from `$INTENT_BIN`, and `burn_subject_provenance.bats` fakes the new line.
- `support.lib`'s `SUPPORT_PATHS` is gone. `support_paths_from <intent>` reads it from the named pair (`cmd/macos` stage from the release pair it stages, `cmd/linux` package from the pair it packages), and refuses when that pair is absent or cannot answer.

### A known reader that moves in WP-03 (vc's ruling, 2026-10-25)

`native/macos/Intent/Intent/Services/VersionService.swift`'s `parse` reads `intent version` for the masthead's version, commit and kind. Read from source, not driven: under the new line its pattern does not match, so it returns the whole line as the version, with commit and kind nil and no crash. The fix is Swift and rides ic's WP-03. Both land in 3.2.7, so no shipped state shows it. The dev Intent.app shows it between this bank's build and ic's landing.

### The judge, named before the run

One heavy run at molt-vc's desk, in the worktree at the bank's tip: `cargo fmt --check`; workspace clippy at `-D warnings`; the whole `intentsvcs`, `intent-cli` and `intentd` suites, `intentd` included because the bank adds files under `crates/*/tests`; `macos_release_assets.bats` and `burn_subject_provenance.bats` with `INTENT_BIN` naming the worktree's build. Then every named reader is driven against that build: `intent --version`, `intent version` and `intentd --version` (shape and byte identity); `intent doctor`'s first line; `intent install --print-runtime-set` and bare `install` (rc 2); `support_paths_from` against the build; `brew.lib`'s `staged_version` over a staged copy of it; `build.d/release`'s `"intent $TARGET "*` match; `burn.sh`'s VERSION capture; and `gen_explorer_shots.sh`'s parse of the line.

wps.title: intent install and the manifest, with doctor's manifest arms
wps.objective: `intent install [--prefix <dir>] [--force] [--managed-by brew]` publishes the runtime set from a dev tree into `<prefix>` as the keg's layout, `<prefix>/bin/{intent,intentd}` and the support paths, and writes `<prefix>/.intent-install`: a header of `# key: value` lines carrying `tool`, `version`, `source_commit` (the full sha the pair was built from) and `managed_by`, then one `shasum -a 256 -c` line per runtime file, paths relative to the root, sorted by `LC_ALL=C sort`. The prefix comes from `--prefix`, else `INTENT_INSTALL_PREFIX`, named once in the docs and read by `install` alone; with neither, install refuses by name. Refused by name, no override: a tree that is not dev; a dirty runtime set (a support path differing from the built commit, or a pair built from a dirty tree or behind HEAD); an existing prefix without `--force`; a prefix whose manifest names another tool or nothing. `--managed-by brew` writes a manifest that refuses `install` and `use` writes into that tree and says to use brew. Doctor in opt and brew checks the manifest body and names every file that drifted; an install in an older form (today's kegs have no manifest at all) is named as old with its remedy: in opt a failure until `install --force`, in brew a note naming `brew upgrade intent`, the tree still answering brew when its root resolves under `$(brew --prefix)/opt/intent/libexec`. Arms: a publish into a scratch prefix round-trips through `shasum -a 256 -c`; each refusal by name; doctor's drift and old-manifest arms over a scratch tree.

wps.title: intent use and the shadow check
wps.objective: `intent use [dev|opt|brew]` is the one verb that points the per-user link set, `~/.local/bin/intent` and `~/.local/bin/intentd`, declared in one function and moved as one because the CLI finds the daemon only beside its own executable. `use dev` and `use opt` point both links at that tree's pair and refuse a tree that is not there, naming the step that makes it (`bin/devbin build all` for dev, `intent install` for opt); `use brew` removes both links and nothing else, so Homebrew's own links answer, and no link means brew; bare `use` reports the tree each link serves and changes nothing, reporting brew when no link is left and the first `intent` on PATH resolves into the keg. Every `use dev|opt` ends with the version line and `intent daemon restart`, so the old tree's daemon does not keep serving. The shadow check, in doctor and in bare `use`, fails when a link in the set exists but is not the first hit on PATH, or when the set is split across trees, naming what shadows or splits it, comparing resolved directories and never path strings. A test-only option names the link directory, defaulting to `~/.local/bin`. The switch governs login shells only: a process started without the login PATH (a launchd-spawned app, cron, Claude Code's hooks and MCP server under the desktop app) may run brew's copy while the maintainer is on dev or opt, and the docs say so; nothing else of Intent's repoints or removes a link. Arms: each of the three switches over a scratch link directory and scratch trees; the bare report; both shadow failures; the refusal naming the missing tree's step.

wps.title: The formula, the release tooling and the docs
wps.objective: The brew tree conforms without a checkout in the keg: the formula goes on installing the signed, notarised release assets (the macOS pair, the Linux static packages, `intent-support.tar.gz`) as ST0081 built it, and after laying them out writes `.intent-install` itself in WP-02's exact form with `managed_by: brew` over the files it placed, which T3 allows since it fixes the form and not the writer. The formula's caveats name `intent use` for a maintainer with a dev or opt tree beside today's `intent bootstrap` line; `test do` keeps running the version line; `bin.install_symlink` keeps linking both binaries into Homebrew's bin. `bin/int brew formula` aligns its verbs to `render <tag> <out>` and `publish`, still rendering from the release's version and per-asset checksums, never a typed tag, commit or checksum. The docs move: `intent/docs/releasing.md` drops `brew unlink intent && brew pin intent && intent daemon restart`, and the cut's smoke step leaves the keg linked; `docs/install.md` names brew alone for a user and gains one maintainer section for dev and opt, with the upgrade procedure per tree (dev: `git pull` then `bin/devbin build all`; opt: `intent install --force` from dev; brew: `brew upgrade intent` under `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, then `intent daemon restart`), since `intent upgrade` is the project verb and is not repurposed. Tests and lint are cargo and bats in the checkout only, so nothing is refused in opt or brew. This package is the cut-facing half: its formula change ships with the first release whose keg carries a manifest, and that release's cut runs doctor on a machine still holding the old keg.

wps.title: The proof, per tree, on rhadamanth and kovacs
wps.objective: The contract's proof, run and recorded as the thread's evidence. On rhadamanth, with the pair built from the thread's tip: `intent use dev`, `intent use opt` (into a scratch prefix published by `intent install`) and `intent use brew` in turn, each followed by the version line, doctor and the shadow check passing, `~/.local/bin` ahead of the first Homebrew bin on PATH as Molt-matts sets it; then `intent use dev` to restore this machine. On kovacs, brew alone: the version line, doctor and the shadow check with no link in `~/.local/bin`, run by kovacs-sysadm on vc's notice after the release carrying WP-04 reaches the tap. devbin's switch proven in this checkout: `bin/devbin doctor` names the install the switch chose and why, in each devbin tree, and `bin/devbin upgrade` reads that install, run in a scratch clone of Intent since it writes the vendored runtime. Every brew probe prefixed with `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, every heavy run booked at molt-vc's desk with START and END by name. The record is the acceptance evidence attached to this thread, each line a measurement with its command.

attachments.text:
# ST0087 design: Intent conforms to the dev, opt and brew contract

Written on 2026-10-25 by vc from Intent's measured column against the contract (2026-10-24, at e6b784790) and the contract as landed. What is marked measured was measured on rhadamanth; the rest is design to be measured before it is built.

## The contract and its one home

The contract has one home, devbin's `docs/dev-opt-brew.md`, landed at Devbin commit aeed31e4 and amended by devbin issues 0213 (the no-manifest brew keg, decision 58) and 0216. Its sections T1 to T10 are cited below by number and never restated; where this document says SAME, Intent follows the section as written, and where it says Intent's reading, the contract already admits it (the compiled-tool readings were Intent's requests, said SAME by all four estates on 2026-10-24 as draft v0.4). hv's rulings that frame it: one approach for Molt, Utilz, Intent and devbin; the user's links first on PATH (option B); this thread third in 3.2.7 after issue 0635 and the devbin v0.1.14 re-vendor (vc decision 71), both landed before this design was written.

## What Intent is, in the contract's terms

Intent is a compiled tool: two binaries, `intent` and `intentd`, plus a support tree the binaries read and exec. Its runtime set (T1) is the pair built from one commit plus the support paths git names: `lib/templates`, `intent/plugins/claude` and `intent/plugins/agents/plugin.json`. Measured: that list exists once today as `SUPPORT_PATHS` in `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/support.lib`, and every release asset takes it from the commit with `git archive` (issue 0626). Under T1 the list lives in the binary as one function, and the packaging reads it from there. Measured by cc on 2026-10-25: the binary holds no copy today (only the root marker `lib/templates`), and `SUPPORT_PATHS` is used by `cmd/macos` (stage coverage, the coverage loop, the provenance blockers, the support-asset build and drift messages), `cmd/linux` (the dirt check), `support.lib`'s own `git archive` and the `macos_release_assets.bats` fixture. Ruled (vc, 2026-10-25, cc's shape): `intent install --print-runtime-set` prints the set one path per line as the verb's first mode, in WP-01, the publish modes following in WP-02 (bare `install` refuses as not built until then); `support.lib` reads it from the pair the caller names, the staged pair for a release and the dev pair for the dev checks, and refuses when that pair is absent. A pair behind HEAD cannot pass those checks anyway, since T2 calls it dirty, so an older binary's list never decides; no text copy and no guard between two homes.

The manifest (T3) is `<root>/.intent-install`. The link set (T5) is `~/.local/bin/intent` and `~/.local/bin/intentd`, moved as one: measured, the CLI finds the daemon only as `intentd` beside its own executable (`intentd_candidates` in intent-cli's `render.rs`) and refuses a stale sibling by its version, so a split set is a real failure.

## T1, the trees

- dev is the git checkout; its runtime is the release pair cargo builds into `native/rust/target/release` (`bin/devbin build all` builds in staging, verifies the pair as a set and promotes by rename) plus the checkout's support paths. The root is found by walking up from the symlink-resolved executable to the first directory holding `lib/templates` (`intentsvcs::install::home`); no environment variable names the tree (`INTENT_HOME` is inert, measured). SAME.
- opt is `intent install --prefix <dir>`, which does not exist today; its layout is the keg's `libexec` layout exactly. The configured place is `INTENT_INSTALL_PREFIX`, declared by the sleeve as Molt's is, read by `install` alone. No default. SAME.
- brew is `$(brew --prefix)/opt/intent/libexec`. Measured keg: `libexec/bin/{intent,intentd}`, `libexec/lib/templates`, `libexec/intent/plugins`, with Homebrew's `bin/intent` and `bin/intentd` as links into it. SAME, already true.
- The compiled-tool reading: `source_commit` is the commit the pair was BUILT from, which in dev can lag HEAD. In the contract.

## T2 and T3, publish and the manifest

`intent install` runs in dev only; from opt or brew it is refused by name. Dirty, for Intent, is: any support path differs from the built commit in git, or the pair's compiled-in stamp names a dirty build or a commit behind HEAD. Refused by name, no override; live project records (`intent/`) never count. An existing prefix is replaced only with `--force` and only over a manifest that says `tool: intent`; anything else is refused. `--managed-by brew` writes a manifest that refuses `install` and `use` writes into that tree. The manifest is T3's exact form; the binaries are checksummed as installed (the signed bytes on macOS), which is what the user has.

The brew tree is published differently and conforms: the formula does not run `intent install` in the keg because the keg has no checkout; it installs release assets (Developer ID signed and notarised binaries on macOS, static musl packages on Linux, the support tarball) and writes the manifest itself in T3's form with `managed_by: brew`. Today's kegs carry no manifest at all: by T3 as amended, a keg whose root resolves under the opt link answers brew with a doctor note naming `brew upgrade intent`, never a failure, until a release whose formula writes the manifest; in opt a prefix with no manifest is not Intent's and `use opt` refuses it.

## T4, tree identity and the version line

One function names the tree, in the contract's order, and every caller asks it; doctor fails on unknown. The line moves from today's `intent <version> (<sha40>) <provenance>` (measured on the dev pair and on the keg's binary) to `intent <version> (<tree>, <sha12>[+dirty]) at <root> <provenance>`. The sha is the built commit, read from the binary, never HEAD at run time; doctor says when HEAD has moved past the build (today's currency check). `+dirty` in dev when the support set differs from the built commit or the pair was built from a dirty tree; never in opt or brew. The trailing provenance word stays (`release` for a release-stamped build, `dev` for a dev build), read by the gate's self-provenance arm and the build's pair verification; readers of the first four fields ignore it. `at <root>` is absolute; for brew it is the opt link, which the tool prints when `current_exe` canonicalises through `Cellar/intent/<version>` to the same directory. When a dev tree's git cannot be read, the sha field says `unknown` and doctor fails saying why.

The readers that move with the line (cc's static measurement of 2026-10-25, driven again against a pair printing the new line at WP-01's judge): the two printers, intent-cli's `spine.rs` and intentd's `main.rs`, become one formatter in intentsvcs that both call; `gen_explorer_shots.sh` in the ST0056 parity tools, which splits the line by position; the Rust pins `version_spellings_agree.rs` and `arguments_do_not_start_a_daemon.rs`; and the bats fixtures that fake the line, `macos_release_assets.bats` and `burn_subject_provenance.bats`. One more, found by cc on 2026-10-25 while re-reading the list for WP-01: the macOS app's `VersionService.swift` parses the line for the masthead's version, commit and kind, and under the new line its match fails, so the whole line shows as the version with commit and kind empty and nothing crashes; it moves in WP-03's Swift half, with `VersionServiceTests` driving the new line, its `+dirty` form, the brew form and T4's `(dev, unknown)` form. Readers of the version field alone (`brew.lib`'s `staged_version`, `build.d/release`, the formula's `test do`) and readers that print or record the whole line survive unchanged. Neither the gate's self-provenance arm nor `verify_pair` reads the line: both read the `[intent-source-commit:...]` marker inside the binary, so the trailing provenance word is read by no shell and stays last at no cost.

## T5, the switch

`intent use [dev|opt|brew]` as WP-03 states it. `use` ends by exec'ing the NEW link set's `intent daemon restart` and printing that binary's line, never a restart in-process: measured by ic on 2026-10-25, `current_exe` is not canonicalised on macOS (the running daemon's argv0 is the link path) and `intentd_candidates` takes its parent, so an in-process restart from the old tree's binary would start the sibling of the old invocation path, or refuse the new link's daemon by version. There is one daemon per user, so every session sees a short gap at the switch. Intent.app, measured by ic on 2026-10-25 from a source read of native/macos/Intent: the app resolves `command -v intent` from one login shell at launch and REALPATHS it, so it holds the tree's own binary rather than the link, and its Restart runs that binary by full path, whose sibling daemon is that tree's; after `use opt` one click would put the daemon back on dev, the "nothing else repoints" rule broken by a GUI process. Ruled (vc, 2026-10-25): the app keeps the link path and follows it live at every spawn (WP-03, a Swift change with the app's tests moved off the realpath pin, ic's), so `use` needs no relaunch of the app and the app's own daemon-status comparison follows the switch; the docs say to relaunch the app once after the release that carries it. `use` relaunching the app is not built. `use` is free as a verb; with prefix inference `intent u` becomes ambiguous beside `upgrade`, which the bank notes. Hooks, skills and templates follow the switch at once in every session, since each hook resolves from the running binary's own install root.

What option B flips for Intent, measured:

1. `intent/docs/releasing.md`'s step `brew unlink intent && brew pin intent && intent daemon restart` goes. Today the keg is unlinked and pinned precisely to keep it off PATH while the dev pair is in use (`brew list --pinned` names intent; `/opt/homebrew/bin/intent` does not exist). Under B the keg stays linked, `brew upgrade intent` may move prod freely, and the user links decide; `bin/int brew smoke --reinstall` leaves the keg linked.
2. Nothing flips for `bin/int` or `bin/devbin`: both are reached by relative path from the checkout.
3. PATH on rhadamanth (measured): `brew shellenv` in `.zprofile` prepends Homebrew's bin after `path_helper`, and it appears twice, so Molt-matts puts `~/.local/bin` ahead of the FIRST `/opt/homebrew/bin` with a prepend. Measured by ic on 2026-10-25: a login shell on rhadamanth already has `~/.local/bin` ahead of both Homebrew bin entries, so the prepend has landed: Molt-matts commits a258ad0 (zshrc, `~/.local/bin` first on PATH, hv's ruling of 2026-10-24) and 91a71ff (prepended in zprofile, so every login shell has it, non-interactive ones included), on Molt-matts' upstream, confirmed by molt-vc on 2026-10-25. A session started before them keeps its old PATH. WP-05's proof depends on it.
4. The hazard the switch cannot see: a process started without the login PATH (the Claude Code desktop app, Chrome's native host, cron) whose PATH has `/opt/homebrew/bin` and not `~/.local/bin` resolves brew's `intent` for Claude Code's hooks (`intent claude hook ...` in `.claude/settings.json`) and for the MCP server (`"command": "intent"` in `.mcp.json`) while the maintainer is on dev. Today those processes find no `intent` there, because the keg is unlinked, and fail loudly; under B they silently run prod. `launchctl getenv PATH` is empty on this machine, so each app inherits its launcher's PATH. The contract names this (T5, what the shadow check cannot see). It is wider than launchd, measured by ic on 2026-10-25: a Claude Code CLI session started by `claude --resume` before the prepend carries `/opt/homebrew/bin` ahead of `~/.local/bin`, so under B its hooks and MCP server run brew's copy until the session is started again from a login shell. Intent's docs say both in the maintainer section (WP-03), WP-05's proof runs from a session started after the prepend, and whether launchd's PATH is set is Molt's decision.

## T6 and T7, upgrading and tests

Intent has no self-upgrade verb and `intent upgrade` is taken (it upgrades a project's `intent/` directory), which T6 allows: the procedure per tree is documented in `docs/install.md`'s maintainer section (WP-04). Intent ships no test or lint verb, so T7 holds by construction; doctor's manifest check in opt and brew is an arm beside the existing currency arm.

## T8, the formula

Rendered, never typed, by `bin/int brew formula` from the release's version and per-asset checksums; the verbs align to `render` and `publish`; the input shape stays assets, not a tag and a revision, because the formula installs assets (T2). `install` links both binaries into Homebrew's bin, `test do` runs the version line, the caveats name `intent bootstrap` (brew's post_install cannot reach the user's HOME) and `intent use`.

## T9, devbin's switch in this checkout

Intent vendors devbin, so this checkout is one of the proof sites for devbin's switch: `bin/devbin doctor` names the install the switch chose and why; `bin/devbin upgrade` reads it. Measured on 2026-10-24: `devbin` resolved only to Homebrew's, with no `~/.local/bin/devbin`; the re-vendor to 0.1.14 landed at 141dcf9ff on 2026-10-25.

## T10, the proof

WP-05 as stated. The Intent proof runs only once `install`, `use`, the manifest and the tree word exist, after the thread's banks land; the kovacs half after the release carrying WP-04 reaches the tap.

## Work packages

- WP-01 The tree function, the runtime set and the version line (T1, T4), M.
- WP-02 `intent install` and the manifest, with doctor's manifest arms (T2, T3), M.
- WP-03 `intent use` and the shadow check (T5), M.
- WP-04 The formula, the release tooling and the docs (T2 brew, T6, T8), S.
- WP-05 The proof (T9, T10), S.

Order: WP-01 first, since every other package reads the tree function and prints the line; WP-02 and WP-03 may proceed in parallel over it; WP-04 after both, since it is the cut-facing half; WP-05 last. Each package is one bank per node, judged whole at molt-vc's desk under the rule that any change under crates/*/tests runs the intentd suite and a surface change runs the workspace suite.
